approval_ref: The active goal requires CRIP to reduce unnecessary model input and manage advanced-model work locally without silently authorizing execution.
notes: Apply the existing deterministic literal page selector to every question in one frozen Reference evaluation.
Return question and page metadata, input-size aggregates, selection warnings and operational blockers without source text, model output or a provider call.
Keep the stable input manifest identity separate from changing readiness status and never treat readiness inspection as execution confirmation.
Add an English-first browser view with safe text rendering while preserving every existing execution path.
Use only synthetic offline acceptance; do not run or claim a stronger-model benchmark.

Implemented a strict 4 MiB metadata-only readiness contract, deterministic input and status identities, whole-task selector reuse, operational blockers, aggregate input scope and an English-first safe browser view without a database migration.

Validated 36 focused backend/browser tests, 24 localization tests and the complete 1,518-test Python suite. Requirements=152, schemas=24; all evidence/model behavior was synthetic and no external provider call was made.
title: Zero-call whole-evaluation input plan and readiness manifest
objective: Let a user inspect the exact whole-task page scope, input size and safe run blockers locally before separately deciding whether to authorize Reference model execution.
